problems.description: Commits compiled build/ output (cli.js, generator.js, .d.ts, sourcemaps) into version control instead of gitignoring it; artifacts must be regenerated from src, creating drift risk and repo bloat.
61 convention violations across index.ts, cache.ts, cli.ts: classes/interfaces not PascalCase, functions not camelCase, constants not UPPER_CASE (measured convention score 0.51).
SonarQube reports +10 code smells and +110 cognitive complexity for 13 added functions, indicating several over-complex functions.
1.6% code duplication introduced across the new modules.
No tests included in session 1 despite +4246 lines of new functionality.

strengths: Clean module separation: cli.ts (entry), parser.ts, generator.ts with a single public generateSite() seam.
Generated HTML escapes user content (htmlEncode for &, <, >, "), mitigating XSS in rendered pages.
Recursive output-dir creation and an index page renderer indicate a complete, functional build path.
commit_reviews.summary: Sound greenfield module structure but dragged down by committing regenerable build artifacts and a 0.51 convention score; note the convention score already captures the style issues while the critical debt is the build/ tree in git.

problems.description: Committed build artifacts and source maps (build/cli.js, build/*.map, build/*.d.ts.map) — generated output and debug mapping files in version control; compile artifacts should be gitignored and regenerated.

Template loading logic (registerPartials, loadTemplates, renderPage) adds ~90 lines in one function region of generator.js; could be extracted into a separate module to match the file-separation pattern of the codebase.
Introduces Handlebars as a new runtime dependency (+1 import) for a feature that could have been a lighter string-based interpolation, expanding the dependency surface.
No test changes accompany the new template-rendering path; behavior is unverified beyond the +590-line code addition.

strengths: Follows the existing CLI parsing pattern: --templates mirrors the established --content/--output argument handling in parseArgs.
Optional templateDir parameter preserves backward compatibility with existing generateSite(pages, outputDir) callers.
SonarQube shows cognitive complexity decreased by -5 with +0 bugs and +0.0% duplications introduced.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, backward-compatible feature addition that mirrors existing CLI patterns and reduces complexity, but is dragged down by committing compiled build artifacts and adding an unextracted ~90-line template loader with no accompanying tests.

problems.description: The new 'serve' branch duplicates the parseDirectory + generateSite + logging sequence already present in the 'build' branch instead of extracting a shared helper (matches duplications +2.9%).
Cognitive complexity +141 from the new server module and CLI dispatch restructure; the startServer/server lifecycle adds a large surface for a single command.
Convention score 0.51 with 61 violations across cli.ts, index.ts, and cache.ts (PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_CASE naming rules) — well below the 0.6 threshold.
No test files in the diff covering the new serve command or the refactored command dispatch.
--port is parsed with parseInt without validation, so an invalid value silently falls back to NaN and the serve behavior becomes undefined.
Compiled build/ artifacts (server.js, *.d.ts, source maps) are committed, adding ~761 lines of generated noise to the diff (consistent with the repo's existing pattern, but inflating review surface).

strengths: The refactor scopes build and serve into explicit command branches, making the dispatch logic clearer than the original implicit flow.
serve reuses the existing parseDirectory/generateSite pipeline rather than forking a parallel implementation.
startServer returns a ServerInstance with close() and rebuild() lifecycle methods, which is a testable, well-shaped API.
Usage text is updated to document both commands and the new --port flag.
commit_reviews.summary: The commit adds a functional serve command by refactoring the CLI dispatch, but it does so at the cost of duplicated build logic, +141 cognitive complexity, and poor convention adherence (0.51), making the change net-negative on quality metrics.

problems.description: 61 naming-convention violations introduced/left in new and modified files (index.ts, cache.ts, cli.ts): classes/interfaces not PascalCase, functions not camelCase, constants not UPPER_CASE; convention score measured at 0.51.
Marked as a 'refactor' yet the diff increases cognitive complexity by +179, adds +6 smells, and +1.8% duplication across +26 files / +884 lines — the opposite of a net simplification.

In the serve branch, `const pages = engine.pages` is captured before `await engine.build()` while the build branch reads `engine.pages.length` after build — inconsistent ordering that risks logging a stale page count if build replaces the array (no bug asserted; matches SonarQube bugs +0).
loadConfigPlugins swallows all errors (including syntax/require failures in ssg.config.js) and silently falls back to defaults, masking real configuration problems.

strengths: Coherent plugin architecture (SSGEngine.register + Markdown/Template/DevServer plugins) decouples core build from content concerns.
Config-driven plugin loading via ssg.config.js (with .default interop) improves extensibility.
Top-level async main() with a .catch handler provides uniform error handling and non-zero exit on failure.
commit_reviews.summary: A conceptually sound plugin-architecture refactor that lands worse on the metrics — +179 cognitive complexity, 6 smells, 1.8% duplication, 61 naming violations (convention 0.51), and an inconsistent page-count read in the serve path.

problems.description: Compiled build artifacts (build/cache.js, build/cache.d.ts, build/cache.d.ts.map) are committed to version control; generated output should be produced by the build step, not tracked.
Convention score 0.51 with 61 violations reported (PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_CASE naming rules across index.ts, cache.ts, cli.ts).
Cognitive complexity increased by +7 in the new caching logic.
computeFileHash and save() use synchronous fs I/O (readFileSync/writeFileSync), which can block the build on large template trees.
Diff is large (+1446 lines) relative to net functional change; most bulk is generated build output rather than authored logic.

strengths: Sound cache-invalidation strategy keyed on content hashes plus a template hash, so stale pages are evicted deterministically.
Graceful handling of corrupted/invalid cache files (try/catch falls back to a fresh cache rather than crashing the build).
Self-contained BuildCache class keeps cache state and serialization encapsulated behind a clear interface.
Net quality improved: smells -3, bugs +0, and total functional lines decreased (-47).
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent and well-encapsulated caching layer that reduces smells, but convention adherence is weak (0.51) and committing compiled build artifacts into the repo introduces avoidable technical debt; note that several reported violations (e.g. 'Classes should use PascalCase' for the correctly-cased BuildCache) look spurious relative to the visible code.

compounding_issues: Session 4's refactor left src/server.ts as dead code in the tree (its logic was copied verbatim into src/plugins/devserver.ts) and it persists unused into session 5, creating a dual-implementation drift risk

The session 4 refactor shipped without updating tests: tests/server.test.ts still imports startServer from the dead src/server.ts, so the new engine.ts + plugins/devserver.ts pipeline has zero test coverage — tests pass against code that is no longer wired in, giving false confidence
Session 4 CLI serve branch captures `const pages = engine.pages` before `await engine.build()` populates it, so it logs '0 pages' after a successful serve
Session 2 kept the legacy HTML-rendering fallbacks (wrapPage/renderPageHtml/renderIndexHtml) alongside the new Handlebars engine, forcing session 5's cache to handle two parallel render paths
Session 5's cache gates every hit on a non-empty template hash (empty when no templates dir), so the incremental cache silently provides no benefit in template-less builds
key_decisions: Session 2: adopting Handlebars with layouts/partials as the theming layer — the first extension point and the seed of the later plugin boundary

Session 4: extracting a hook-based plugin engine (SSGEngine with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) plus ssg.config.js — the pivotal architectural pivot that refactored markdown/template/devserver into interchangeable plugins
Session 3: building a dev server with live-reload via an injected WebSocket reload script (chokidar + ws) directly into generated HTML rather than using a framework
Session 5: incremental build cache keyed on SHA-256 content and template hashes threaded through parser and generator, plus orphaned-output cleanup in generateSite
Session 1: separating parser/generator/CLI into three single-purpose modules with a shared types.ts — the stable seams all later sessions built on
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. Session 1 delivered a clean, minimal core (parser/generator/CLI) with focused tests; session 2 added a real feature (Handlebars templating) and grew the test suite; session 3 integrated a dev server with live reload and accompanying tests. Session 4 was a structural upgrade to a plugin architecture — genuinely better organization and configurability — but it was the weak point of the arc, introducing duplicated dead code (server.ts) and leaving the new plugin pipeline untested while old tests continued passing against the obsolete module. Session 5 recovered the trajectory by adding the most carefully engineered feature (an incremental cache spanning parser/engine/generator with the largest test file at 667 lines), showing the agent understood and reused the earlier architecture. Net arc: rising, with one refactor dip that accrued modest debt.
story_review.summary: A textbook five-session progression (core → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) with high coherence and an improving quality arc, slightly marred by a session 4 refactor that left dead code and untested plugin paths behind.
